Role Summary:
This role makes the frontline sales force a competitive advantage: the right reps and Frontline Sales Managers (FSMs) hired, productive quickly, performing consistently, and led by managers who deliver both revenue and profit.

Purpose. Revenue depends on thousands of small-outlet visits executed well every day. The HRBP ensures the Commercial Department has the people, managers, and organization to deliver its revenue and profit plan. This means owning the frontline talent system end to end (hire, ramp, perform, develop) and advising Commercial leadership on every major people and organization decision.

Key Accountabilities:

1. Strategic partnership with Commercial leadership (15%)
• Act as the Commercial Director's primary advisor on people and organization; sit on the Commercial leadership team and attend monthly and quarterly business reviews.
• Translate the annual commercial plan (revenue, volume, numeric distribution, outlet coverage, gross margin) into a people plan: headcount, route coverage, capability, and people cost.
• Maintain a sales force workforce model: outlets per rep, reps per FSM, vacancy and attrition assumptions, and the revenue cost of reps still ramping.
• Lead organization design for sales structure changes, such as new regions or channels, route re-cuts, pre-sell versus van sales, and direct versus distributor coverage.
• Partner with Finance and Sales Operations on sales incentive schemes; review them for motivation, fairness, affordability, and compliance, and help FSMs explain them.
• Bring people data into commercial decisions, for example linking vacancies, tenure, and FSM turnover to route and territory results.

2. Attract and hire the right frontline talent (20%)
• Define success profiles for rep and FSM roles based on what top performers here actually do (e.g., route discipline, rapport with shop owners, basic sales math, reliability, resilience).
• With Talent Acquisition, run a structured high-volume hiring process: channels that work in Cambodia (Facebook and Telegram groups, provincial networks, referrals, universities and vocational schools), practical assessments (shop-owner role-play, ride-along, numeracy test), and structured interviews.
• Build pipelines ahead of demand so priority routes are not left uncovered.
• Select FSMs on people leadership, not just personal sales results; build a promotion path from rep to senior rep to FSM with a readiness assessment.
• Track quality of hire (90-day retention, time to productivity) by source and by hiring manager, and fix what the data shows.
• Where reps are employed by distributors, set hiring standards and support distributors to apply them.

3. Onboard and ramp new hires (15%)
• Design a 30-60-90 day ramp program for reps: product and brand knowledge, sales systems (e.g., handheld or SFA app), outlet call standards, and ride-alongs with top performers.
• Agree staged ramp targets and incentive treatment for new reps with Sales and Finance.
• Equip FSMs to deliver the field portion with checklists, coaching guides, and day 30, 60, and 90 check-ins.
• Run a separate transition program for new FSMs: moving from seller to manager, team P&L basics, coaching, and performance conversations.
• Measure ramp time and early attrition by hiring cohort, and improve the program each cycle.

4. Manage performance and remediate (20%)
• Design a sales-specific performance framework with balanced measures: revenue and volume versus target, profitability and mix, distribution, call compliance, strike rate, collections, and conduct.
• Build a remediation program for struggling reps and FSMs with early-warning triggers, diagnosis of the cause, a tailored plan, and fair documented outcomes consistent with Cambodian labor law.
• Escalate underperformance caused by territory, stock, or pricing to Commercial leadership rather than treating it as individual failure.
• Lead talent reviews and calibration for the Commercial Department to identify top performers, high potentials, and at-risk talent.
• Manage sales force employee relations cases (e.g., cash handling, stock discrepancies, customer complaints, misconduct) with fair investigations.

5. Build FSM capability and retain talent (15%)
• Maintain succession plans for FSM roles and above.
• Create career paths that let strong reps grow without having to become managers (e.g., senior rep grades, key outlet specialist roles).
• Analyze attrition drivers (pay and incentive payout, manager, workload, travel) using exit and stay interviews, and act on them.
• Run field-friendly engagement pulses and recognition tied to commercial priorities.

6. Partner with Product & Brand (10%)
• Serve as HRBP for Product & Brand at all levels, from brand assistants to marketing leadership.
• Lead organization design, workforce planning, hiring, and talent reviews for marketing roles.
• Build capabilities such as consumer insight, brand P&L management, digital marketing, and trade marketing.
• Strengthen Brand and Sales collaboration: shared forums, launch readiness (sales force trained before a launch), and rotations between sales and marketing to widen the commercial bench.

7. Employee relations, compliance, and governance (5%)
• Apply Cambodian labor law and company policy consistently, including contract types, probation, working hours for field staff, NSSF, seniority payments, and termination.
• Ensure field allowances (fuel, phone, per diem), incentives, and deductions are documented, fair, and compliant.
• Manage the Commercial HR budget and keep sales force data in the HRIS accurate.

Qualifications and competencies:

Education:
• Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, or a related field.
• HR certification or a master's degree is an advantage.

Experience:
• 7+ years in HR, including 3+ years as an HRBP or senior HR generalist supporting a large sales force in FMCG, beverages, telecoms, consumer finance, or distribution.
• Hands-on experience with high-volume frontline hiring, onboarding programs, and performance improvement processes.
• Exposure to sales incentive schemes and sales organization design.
• Experience in sales, sales operations, or a field role is a strong plus.

Knowledge:
• Working knowledge of Cambodian labor law and NSSF requirements.
• Understanding of general trade sales KPIs (e.g., numeric distribution, strike rate, lines per call, drop size) and how FSMs influence team profitability.
• Strong Excel and people analytics skills; experience with an HRIS.

Languages:
• Fluent Khmer and professional English, spoken and written.

Competencies:
• Commercial acumen: understands how the business makes money and speaks the language of sales and marketing.
• Data-driven judgment: uses people and sales data to diagnose problems and prove impact.
• Influence and credibility: challenges senior leaders constructively and earns trust from FSMs and reps.
• Coaching: builds manager capability rather than solving every problem personally.
• Field presence: spends real time in markets and outlets, not just at head office.
• Fairness and courage: handles underperformance and misconduct firmly, consistently, and respectfully.
• Pace and resilience: delivers in a fast, target-driven environment.

Working conditions:
• Frequent travel to provinces, including overnight trips and occasional early-morning route visits.
Senior HR Specialist, Talent Development and Compensation & Benefits
Phnom Penh, Cambodia

Role Summary:
This company-wide specialist role helps deploy the company's existing Lean Management System and develops employees through it, while owning compensation and benefits, talent and performance management, and organization design. It is part of a decentralized HR structure: compliance, Ministry of Labor reporting, commercial HR, and factory HR are handled by other specialists. The role is a hands-on doer focused on building employee capability and improving business results, not an administrative or compliance role.

Key Accountabilities:
1. Learning, development and lean deployment (40%)
• Lead the deployment of the company's existing Lean Management System across departments and develop employees through it (the role deploys the system; it does not design a new one).
• Follow up after training: check that methods are applied in daily work, review results, and drive continuous improvement.
• Build employee capability and career development through a consistent management system across departments.
• Run the annual training needs analysis and manage the training plan and budget.
• Deliver or source training programs, including onboarding and manager development.
• Measure training effectiveness and keep training records.

2. Talent and performance management (20%)
• Coordinate the performance review cycle and link results to pay and development.
• Facilitate talent reviews and succession plans for critical roles.
• Build career paths for key job families.

3. Organization design (15%)
• Go beyond maintaining the organization chart: review structures across the company and recommend changes.
• Identify missing positions, staffing gaps, excess management layers, and inappropriate reporting lines.
• Advise on the right balance between frontline employees and managers.

4. Compensation and reward (15%)
• Maintain job grades and salary bands, benchmarked against the Cambodian market – work with agency.
• Review market rates and advise on company-wide salary adjustments; lead the annual salary review with Finance, within the approved budget.
• Review and advise on bonus and incentive schemes for fairness and affordability; commercial incentive programs remain owned by the commercial team.

5. HR operations and employee relations (5%)
• Advise managers and employees on HR policies, contracts, and probation under the Cambodian Labor Law.
• Handle employee relations cases and disciplinary matters fairly.
• Compliance and Ministry of Labor reporting stay with the Compliance function; this role advises and serves as backup only.

6. HR data and reporting (5%)
• Keep HR data accurate and produce monthly HR reports.
• Use people data to support decisions on pay, attrition, and training.

Qualifications and competencies:

Education:
• Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, or a related field is preferred but not required; capability and results matter more than degrees.
• HR or lean certification (e.g., CIPD, SHRM, Lean Six Sigma) is a plus.

Experience:
• At least 7 years in HR, C&B, L&D, or operational excellence as a guide.
• Practical experience with a Lean Management System is strongly preferred. Exceptionally smart, fast-learning.
• Hands-on experience with salary reviews, benchmarking, and training programs.
• Proven track record of completing work and delivering measurable results.

Knowledge and skills:
• Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) and structured problem solving, including A3 thinking.
• Strong execution: gets the job done with ownership, follow-up, and sound judgment.
• Lean tools: Kaizen, value-stream mapping, Kata, visual management, gemba walks, and daily management.
• Meeting facilitation, presentations, proposal writing, and project management.
• Cambodian Labor Law, NSSF.
• Strong Excel skills and experience with an HRIS (HR Systems) and payroll system.
• Fluent Khmer and professional English.

Competencies:
• Smart, proactive, and driven: learns quickly, takes initiative, and pushes for results.
• Hands-on doer: applies the methods personally and earns credibility through results, not only training.
• Analytical: turns pay and people data into clear recommendations.
• Integrity: handles salary and personal data confidentially and consistently.
• Communication: explains pay decisions clearly and delivers engaging training.

Modern Trade Sales Manager
Modern Trade

Modern Trade Account Management:
• Build and maintain strong relationships with key modern trade customers and buyers.
• Plan and implement sales and promotional activities to achieve business objectives.
• Negotiate shelf space, displays, and promotional support with store chains.
• Monitor and improve in-store product visibility and availability.

Sales & Performance Management:
• Achieve monthly and quarterly sales targets by store and by product category.
• Monitor and analyze sales data, stock levels, and sell-out performance.
• Identify sales growth opportunities and recommend actions for improvement.

Team Supervision:
• Lead, coach, and monitor a team of sales reps or merchandisers.
• Plan daily store visits and route plans for team members.
• Conduct regular in-store training and performance evaluations.

Execution & Merchandising:
• Ensure excellent execution of planograms, displays, and promotions.
• Coordinate with marketing and logistics to ensure timely delivery of POS materials and stocks.
• Prevent out-of-stock situations and ensure stock rotation (FIFO).

Market Intelligence & Reporting:
• Monitor competitor activities, promotions, and pricing within modern trade.
• Share timely insights with internal sales and marketing teams.
• Track KPIs such as active store, sales vs. target, availability, and coverage.

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field.
• 2+ years of experience in sales coordination or account management, preferably in FMCG.
• Proven experience managing modern trade channels such as supermarkets, hypermarkets, and key accounts.
• Familiarity with modern trade and pharmacy sales channels.
• Strong communication and negotiation skills.
• Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
• Ability to analyze sales data and develop actionable insights.
• Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
Area Sales Manager
Sales Leadership

Sales Planning and Strategy:
• Develop and implement sales plans to achieve company goals within the assigned area.
• Monitor market dynamics, competitor activities, and customer needs to identify new opportunities.
• Prepare accurate sales forecasts and ensure efficient territory coverage.

Team Leadership and Development:
• Lead, train, and guide the sales team to meet individual and team targets.
• Monitor team performance and provide regular feedback and coaching.
• Support professional development to enhance the team’s selling and negotiation skills.

Customer Relationship Management:
• Build and maintain strong partnerships with key customers, distributors, and retailers.
• Negotiate contracts, pricing, and promotional activities to maximize business growth.
• Ensure excellent customer service and resolve any issues promptly.

Sales Execution and Operations:
• Supervise daily sales activities and ensure the proper implementation of trade marketing programs.
• Ensure product visibility, stock availability, and proper merchandising across outlets.
• Collaborate with other departments to ensure smooth coordination and execution of sales plans.

Reporting and Analysis:
• Review sales reports and analyze performance against targets.
• Identify gaps or potential areas for improvement and recommend action plans.
• Manage area budgets effectively and ensure compliance with company standards.

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, or a related discipline.
• At least 3 to 5 years of experience in a sales leadership role, preferably in FMCG, retail, or distribution.
• Proven ability to achieve and exceed sales goals.
• Strong leadership, communication, and negotiation skills.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint.
• Willingness to travel frequently and work under pressure.
